Date: 2023-11-13
PATENT
REMARKS:
In response to the Office Action mailed August 11, 2023, claims 5, 18, and 20 have been amended. No new matter has been introduced. Accordingly, claims 1-20 remain pending.
In the Office Action, the drawings and Abstract were objected to. In addition, claims 5-7 and 18-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as indefinite. Finally, claims 1 and 5-10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by International Publication No. WO 2000/ 029287 ("Syta"), claim 11 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over Syta reference in view of U.S. Patent No. 3,714,987 ("Mattson"), claims 2-4, 12-14, 18, and 19 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over Syta in view of Mattson and U.S. Publication No. 2012/ 0018569 ("Toni"), claims 11 and 15-17 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over Syta in view of Mattson and U.S. Patent No. 2,973,923 ("the Sznycer"), and claims 11 and 20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as unpatentable over Syta in view of Mattson and "the Rugged and Economic H215 Ready for the U.S. Market" ("Airbus NPL"). Because none of the cited references, either alone or in combination, disclose, teach, or suggest the subject matter of the present claims, the rejections should be withdrawn.
Objections to the Drawings and Abstract
First, with respect to the objections to the drawings, submitted herewith are replacement sheets replacing original FIGS. 5 and 19-21. No new matter has been introduced.
Turning to the objections to the Abstract, although Applicant submits that the original language is proper, in order to advance prosecution, the terms "comprises" and "comprising" have been replaced with "includes" and "including," respectively.
PATENT
Claim Rejections under 35 U.S. Code § 112(b)
With respect to the § 112(b) rejections, claim 5 was rejected as the term "the underside of the fuselage" lacks proper antecedent basis. It is respectfully submitted that one of ordinary skill in the art would understanding that there is only one underside of the fuselage of a helicopter. As such, we respectfully submit that the term is clear and would be understood to be clear by one of ordinary skill in the art. Nevertheless, in the interest of advancing prosecution, claim 5 is amended to recite "an underside of the fuselage of the helicopter".
Claim 18 was rejected as the term "the rod" lacks proper antecedent basis. Claim 18 is amended to depend from claim 12. We respectfully submit that the objection against claim 18 is now moot in light of this amendment.
Finally, claim 20 was rejected in light of the term "Super Puma". Claim 20 is amended to recite "wherein the helicopter is a Eurocopter AS332, Airbus H215 or Airbus H225." Applicant respectfully submits that the objection against claim 20 is now moot in light of this amendment.
Claim Rejections under 35 U.S. Code § 102(a)(1)
Claims 1 and 5-10 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by the WO 2000/029287 ("Syta"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Applicant respectfully submits that Syta fails to disclose or suggest at least "A tank
assembly for a helicopter, the tank assembly comprising... an attachment mechanism attached to the upper frame structure and configured to engage a main rotor transmission of the helicopter to suspend therefrom" as recited in claim 1 of the present application (emphasis added).
On page 5 of the Office Action, the Examiner asserts that the supports 1 and/or
connecting pieces 2 would be capable of being effectively coupled to and engaged with a main
PATENT
rotor transmission, and references page 1, lines 14-17, and FIGS.1-3 of Syta. Applicant respectfully disagrees. Page 1, lines 14-17 of Syta simply states that the tank is fixed to the lower part of the fuselage using the supports 1 and connecting pieces 2. There is no teaching or suggestion in Syta of any of the supports 1 and/or connecting pieces 2 being capable of coupling to or being engaged with a main rotor transmission of the helicopter. In fact, Syta makes no mention of a main rotor transmission at all. Syta does make it clear that the supports 1 and connecting pieces 2 are fixed to the lower part of the fuselage of the helicopter, which is clearly not the main rotor transmission.
In view of the above, Applicant respectfully submits that Syta fails to disclose or suggest each and every feature of claim 1 of the present application.
Applicant also respectfully submits that dependent claims 5-10 are not anticipated by Syta at least by virtue of their dependencies on claim 1.
Regarding claim 7, the Examiner asserts that "the upper panel 3 includes a central
portion or region between the forward and rearward end portions, and the connecting pieces 2 are located in the central portion". Contrary to the Examiner's assertion, the connecting pieces 2 of Syta are located at the forward and rearward end portions of the upper panel 3, and clearly not in the central portion of the upper panel 3.
Claim Rejections under 35 U.S. Code § 103
Claim 11 was rejected under 35 U.S. Code § 103 as being unpatentable over Syta and US 3,714,987 ("Mattson"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. Applicant respectfully submits that Syta fails to disclose or suggest at least "a tank assembly comprising... an attachment mechanism attached to the upper frame structure and engaged with a main rotor
PATENT
transmission of the helicopter to suspend therefrom," as recited in claim 11 of the present application, for similar reasons discussed above for claim 1.
Mattson fails to remedy these deficiencies. Mattson discloses a helicopter with a fire
suppression system including a water tank 32 with a cargo hook engaging swivel 44 that engages the cargo hook 42 of the helicopter 20. However, the cargo hook 42 is not the main rotor transmission of the helicopter 20, nor is the cargo hook 42 connected to the main rotor transmission of the helicopter 20. In fact, there is no disclosure or suggestion in Mattson of any part of the water tank 32 being capable of engaging with the main rotor transmission of the helicopter 20.
Accordingly, there is simply no motivation, nor would it have been obvious, for one of ordinary skill in the art to manipulate the arrangements of Syta and Mattson against their specific teachings in order to arrive at the invention defined in claim 11 of the present application. Applicant also submits that even if one of ordinary skill in the art could be reasonably expected to combine the disclosures of Syta and Mattson (which the Applicant denies), such a combination would still not arrive at the invention defined in claim 11 of the present application.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 11 is patentable in view of Syta and Mattson.
Claims 2-4 were rejected under 35 U.S. Code § 103 as being unpatentable over Syta, Mattson and US 2012/018569 ("Toni"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.
Claims 2-4 directly or indirectly depend from claim 1, and/or include all of the limitations of claim 1. As discussed above, Syta fails to teach or suggest at least "A tank assembly for a helicopter, the tank assembly comprising... an attachment mechanism attached to the upper frame structure and configured to engage a main rotor transmission of the helicopter
PATENT
to suspend therefrom," as recited in claim 1 of the present application. Mattson and Toni fail to remedy these deficiencies.
Regarding claim 4, the Examiner asserts that the combination of Syta, Mattson and Toni discloses a fastener for securing the gimbal head to the rod, wherein the aperture of the gimbal head and the aperture of the lower end portion of the rod are aligned and fixed by the fastener, and references FIGS. 2B, 2C, 3 and 5 of Toni (incorrectly referred as Mattson in the Office Action). Applicant respectfully disagrees.
Toni discloses that the lower frame interface 36 is affixed directly to the frame 42 of the airframe 14, and not the tension member 40 itself (see Toni, paras. [0022]-[0023]), as required by claim 4 of the present application.
Accordingly, even if one of ordinary skill in the art could be reasonably expected to combine the disclosures of Syta, Mattson and Toni (which the Applicant denies), such a combination would still not arrive at the invention defined in claim 4 of the present application.
Claims 12-14 and 18-19 were rejected under 35 U.S. Code § 103 as being unpatentable
over Syta, Mattson and Toni. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. Claims 12-14 and 18- 19 directly or indirectly depend from claim 11, and/or include all of the limitations of claim 11. As discussed above, Syta fails to teach or suggest at least "a tank assembly comprising...an attachment mechanism attached to the upper frame structure and engaged with a main rotor transmission of the helicopter to suspend therefrom," as recited in claim 11 of the present application.
Mattson and Toni fail to remedy these deficiencies. Regarding claim 14, the Examiner asserts that the combination of Syta, Mattson and Toni discloses a fastener for securing the gimbal head to the rod, wherein the aperture of the gimbal head and the aperture of the lower end
PATENT
portion of the rod are aligned and fixed by the fastener, and references FIGS. 2B, 2C, 3 and 5 of Toni (incorrectly referred as Mattson in the Office Action). Applicant respectfully disagrees.
Toni discloses that the lower frame interface 36 is affixed directly to the frame 42 of the airframe 14, and not the tension member 40 itself (see Toni, paras. [0022]-[0023]), as required by claim 14 of the present application.
Accordingly, even if one of ordinary skill in the art could be reasonably expected to combine the disclosures of Syta, Mattson and Toni (which the Applicant denies), such a combination would still not arrive at the invention defined in claim 14 of the present application.
Regarding claims 18 and 19, Toni discloses that the upper clevis 76 of the tension
member 40 is mounted to the swing arm 72 of the upper frame interface 38 which is fixed to the frame 42. However, the tension member 40 is not directly fixed to the main rotor transmission 12 as required by claim 19 of the present application.
Accordingly, even if one of ordinary skill in the art could be reasonably expected to combine the disclosures of Syta, Mattson and Toni (which the Applicant denies), such a combination would still not arrive at the invention defined in claims 18 and 19 of the present application.
Claims 11 and 15-17 are rejected under 35 U.S. Code § 103 as being unpatentable over Syta and US 2,973,923 ("Sznycer"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. As discussed above, Syta fails to disclose or suggest at least "a tank assembly comprising...an attachment mechanism attached to the upper frame structure and engaged with a main rotor transmission of the helicopter to suspend therefrom," as recited in claim 11 of the present application.
Sznycer fails to remedy these deficiencies. Sznycer discloses a helicopter with a centrally located cargo space capable of supporting a cargo basket 36 or a container 45. The cargo basket
PATENT
36 or container 45 is suspended from a cargo release hook 38 (See Sznycer, Fig. 4). However, the cargo release hook 38 is not the main rotor transmission of the helicopter, nor is the cargo release hook 38 connected to the main rotor transmission of the helicopter. In fact, there is no disclosure or suggestion in Sznycer of any part of the cargo basket 36 or container 45 being capable of engaging the main rotor transmission of the helicopter. The Examiner broadly asserts that since the cargo release hook 38 is mounted to the longitudinal portion of the frame work body 10, and the longitudinal portion serves as the main rotor transmission (which the Applicant denies), the upper panel 3 in Syta would be attached, either directly or indirectly to the main rotor transmission via the cargo hook 38 in Sznycer. Applicant respectfully disagrees and believes that this conclusion is an overreach of the teachings of Syta and Sznycer. One of ordinary skill in the art would understand that the airframe is separate to the main rotor transmission of the helicopter. Moreover, the longitudinal portion of the frame work body 10 that the Examiner relies upon is not even close to the main rotor transmission of the helicopter, with the main rotor transmission in Sznycer being disposed above the pylon 11 of the body 10.
Accordingly, there is simply no motivation, nor would it have been obvious, for one of ordinary skill in the art to manipulate the arrangements of Syta and Sznycer against their specific teachings in order to arrive at the invention defined in claim 11 of the present application. Applicant also submits that even if one of ordinary skill in the art could be reasonably expected to combine the disclosures of Syta and Sznycer (which the Applicant denies), such a combination would still not arrive at the invention defined in claim 11 of the present application.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 11 is patentable in view of Syta and Sznycer.
PATENT
Claims 15-17 directly or indirectly depend from claim 11, and/or include all of the
limitations of claim 11. Accordingly, dependent claims 15-17 are also believed to be patentable in view of Syta and Sznycer.
Claims 11 and 20 were rejected under 35 U.S. Code § 103 as being unpatentable over Syta and NPL entitled "The rugged and economic H215 ready for the U.S. market" ("Airbus NPL"). Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. As discussed above, Syta fails to disclose or suggest at least "a tank assembly comprising.. .an attachment mechanism attached to the upper frame structure and engaged with a main rotor transmission of the helicopter to suspend therefrom," as recited in claim 11 of the present application.
Applicant submits that Airbus NPL fails to remedy these deficiencies. Airbus NPL fails to disclose or suggest any use of the main rotor transmission, let alone suspending any objects from the main rotor transmission. Contrary to the Examiner's assertion, there is simply no hint or suggestion in Airbus NPL to even consider having an attachment mechanism that is engaged with the main rotor transmission of the helicopter to suspend therefrom.
Accordingly, there is simply no motivation, nor would it have been obvious, for one of ordinary skill in the art to manipulate the arrangements of Syta and Airbus NPL against their specific teachings in order to arrive at the invention defined in claim 11 of the present application.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 11 is patentable in view of Syta and Airbus NPL.
Claim 20 directly depends from claim 11, and includes all of the limitations of claim 11. Accordingly, dependent claim 20 is also believed to be patentable in view of Syta and Airbus
NPL.
In view of the foregoing, it is submitted that the claims now presented in this application define patentable subject matter over the cited prior art. Accordingly, reconsideration and allowance of the application is requested.
The Commissioner is authorized to charge any fees due for the filing of this Response, and to credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account No. 50-1105 (Vista IP Law Group LLP).
